subject: Post-incident: data custody, region residency, and deletion checklist
messages:
From: Chris Liao <chris.liao@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Yoon <monica.yoon@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident evidence: residency & deletion questions

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick help yesterday. Our security team has one follow-up set of questions after the incident closure:

1) For the session logs and raw inference traces you preserved, can you confirm the AWS region where those artifacts are stored and whether any copies exist outside that region?

2) We need a retention window recommendation for the preserved slices for our compliance team (HIPAA review). We expect regulators may request a subset of records — how long do you suggest Redwood keep the preserved forensic slices vs. the standard 90-day log retention?

3) What is the exact deletion workflow once we request a purge for scoped records? We need the ability to request targeted deletions and to receive a confirmation manifest.

Could someone on your side outline the custody steps and provide export formats (tar/csv/pdf recommended) so our legal team can sign off.

Appreciate it —
Chris
Security Ops, Acme Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Chris Liao <chris.liao@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Yoon <monica.yoon@acmehealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident evidence: residency & deletion questions

Hi Chris —

Thanks — below is a concise playbook we can follow. Looping Sean for technical steps and Marissa for legal/custody language.

High level answers:
- Storage region: the preserved forensic exports for your incident are currently staged in us-west-2 and no automatic cross-region replication is enabled for those artifacts.
- Recommended retention: for HIPAA-sensitive slices we typically recommend 2 years of preservation for incident-related evidence unless your legal requires otherwise; standard operational logs remain on a 90-day rolling retention.
- Deletion workflow: targeted purge requests go through an authenticated ticket, we produce a deletion manifest and perform a verifiable wipe (cryptographic shredding + metadata update).

Action items I will own:
1) Share a custody manifest template and a sample evidence index (attachments).
2) Coordinate the export (tar + CSV index) and secure transfer link.
3) Produce a deletion confirmation record when purge is requested.

Sean / Marissa — can you confirm the export checklist and the timeline for delivering the tarball + manifest?

Thanks,
Vanessa
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Chris Liao <chris.liao@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident evidence: residency & deletion questions

On Tue, Jan 10, 2028 at 10:03 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sean / Marissa — can you confirm the export checklist and the timeline for delivering the tarball + manifest?

Chris / Vanessa — technical plan and timeline below.

Export checklist (what we can deliver):
- Compressed tar.gz containing: raw session logs (JSONL), inference traces (anonymized token-level entries where permitted), and system metrics for the incident window.
- evidence_slice_index.csv: row-per-slice with slice_id, start_ts, end_ts, retention_tag, sha256.
- chain_of_custody_manifest.pdf: signed internal handoff record.

Residency note: artifacts will remain in us-west-2 S3 with server-side encryption (KMS) and a bucket policy that prevents public access. We do not replicate these exported artifacts to other regions unless explicitly requested in writing.

Deletion workflow (targeted):
1) Customer submits ticket with slice_ids to delete and authentication (SAML assertion or signed POA).
2) Engineering runs a scoped deletion job that removes object versions and performs an overwrite where feasible; we record pre- and post-operation hashes.
3) We provide a deletion_manifest.csv listing deleted object keys, timestamps, and cryptographic proof entries.
4) Final confirmation email and update to your retention dashboard.

Timeline: We can produce the export + manifest within 48 hours after authorization; deletion jobs can be scheduled and completed within 24–72 hours depending on slice size and cross-service dependencies.

Let me know if Acme needs the artifacts quarantined to a customer-controlled S3 (we can arrange a secure transfer).

—Sean
Senior Incident Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Chris Liao <chris.liao@acmehealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident evidence: residency & deletion questions

On Tue, Jan 10, 2028 at 11:08 AM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> Deletion workflow (targeted):
> 1) Customer submits ticket with slice_ids to delete and authentication (SAML assertion or signed POA).

Chris / team — adding a few legal controls and records we'd need to finalize before performing deletions:
- Signed deletion approval (DocuSign or equivalent) from Acme authorizing the exact slice_ids. We need the signature from an authorized signatory on your side.
- Confirmation of residency policy exception (if you want data moved or escrowed to another region prior to deletion).
- Retention override window stated in the approval (for auditability).

Also: for HIPAA purposes, please confirm whether the preserved slices must be retained in the US only or if Acme permits movement to a sealed customer export (we'll not transfer without explicit consent).

I attached a sample chain_of_custody_manifest and the evidence index format for your legal review.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Yoon <monica.yoon@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident evidence: residency & deletion questions

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from Acme legal/security:

- We will sign the deletion approval via DocuSign; please send the DocuSign envelope for deletion of slice_ids: S-20280110-a1, S-20280110-a2.
- Acme requests that preserved slices remain in us-west-2 for 18 months (HIPAA audit risk tolerance).
- If Redwood offers an option to escrow a read-only export to our customer-controlled S3 (us-west-2) that would be preferred before deletion; please include instructions and IAM steps if possible.

Can we get an export link and the chain_of_custody draft today? We need to include those in our audit packet.

Regards,
Monica Yoon
Senior Counsel, Acme Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Chris Liao <chris.liao@acmehealth.com>, Monica Yoon <monica.yoon@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident evidence: residency & deletion questions

Monica / Chris —

Summary and next steps (owned by Redwood):
1) Export: Sean will deliver a secure, pre-signed transfer link with logs_export_20280110.tar.gz, evidence_slice_index.csv, and chain_of_custody_manifest.pdf by EOD today. (Attachment stubs sent with this thread.)
2) Retention: We will tag the slices with an "acme_preserve_202801" retention policy for 18 months in us-west-2 per your request.
3) Escrow: We can push a read-only copy to your customer S3 bucket; Sean will send a minimal IAM role and secure transfer steps.
4) Deletion: We will only execute deletions after we receive a DocuSign-signed deletion approval listing exact slice IDs. Once complete, Redwood will provide deletion_manifest.csv with cryptographic proof.

Deliverables attached: chain_of_custody_manifest.pdf (draft), evidence_slice_index.csv (sample), logs_export_20280110.tar.gz (metadata stub). Please review and confirm the DocuSign envelope recipient for the deletion approval.

I'll follow up once the pre-signed link is created.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
